cases.purpose: spawn allocates a PTY and starts the child as a session leader with the PTY as its controlling terminal (child self-check: getsid==pid, isatty, tcgetpgrp==getpgrp, /dev/tty opens); FD_VAR is an open descriptor and PID_VAR is the child's own pid; the prompt is matched and captured with -V; sendline reaches the child as 'alice\n' and is echoed by the line discipline; a CR sent with send arrives as NL (ICRNL); after the child exits, expect returns 2 and eof 0; close returns the exit status 7 and the pid no longer exists.
cases.script:
expect log_user off
expect spawn /usr/bin/python3 rt.py dialog -h fd -h pid; echo "spawn=$?" > spawn
[[ $fd =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -e /proc/self/fd/$fd ]] && echo fd-open >> spawn
[[ $pid =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] && echo pid-numeric >> spawn
expect expect "$fd" 'leader=[a-z]+ ctty=[a-z]+ pid=[0-9]+'$'\r' -t 10 -V info; echo "info=$?" >> spawn
info=${info%$'\r'}
[[ ${info##*pid=} == "$pid" ]] && echo pid-is-child >> spawn || echo pid-differs >> spawn
printf '%s\n' "${info% pid=*}" >> spawn
expect expect "$fd" 'name\? $' -t 10 -V prompt; printf 'rc=%s prompt=[%s]\n' $? "$prompt" > prompt
expect sendline "$fd" alice; echo "sendline=$?" > line
expect expect "$fd" "got='[^']*'" -t 10 -V got; printf 'rc=%s %s\n' $? "$got" >> line
expect expect "$fd" $'alice\r' -t 0; echo "echoed=$?" >> line
expect expect "$fd" 'cmd\? $' -t 10; echo "cmd=$?" >> line
expect send "$fd" $'bob\r'; echo "send=$?" >> line
expect expect "$fd" "got2='[^']*'" -t 10 -V got2; printf 'rc=%s %s\n' $? "$got2" >> line
expect expect "$fd" never-printed -t 10; echo "expect-at-eof=$?" > end
expect eof "$fd" -t 10; echo "eof=$?" >> end
expect close "$fd" "$pid"; echo "close=$?" >> end
[[ -e /proc/$pid ]] && echo child-present >> end || echo child-gone >> end

files.rt.py:
import os, signal, sys, time
def w(s): os.write(1, s.encode())
mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == 'dialog':
    leader = os.getsid(0) == os.getpid() and os.isatty(0) and os.tcgetpgrp(0) == os.getpgrp()
    try:
        os.close(os.open('/dev/tty', os.O_RDWR)); ctty = 'yes'
    except OSError:
        ctty = 'no'
    w('leader=%s ctty=%s pid=%d\n' % ('yes' if leader else 'no', ctty, os.getpid()))
    w('name? ')
    w('got=%r\n' % os.read(0, 100).decode())
    w('cmd? ')
    w('got2=%r\n' % os.read(0, 100).decode())
    sys.exit(7)
if mode == 'killself':
    w('ready\n')
    os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGTERM)
    time.sleep(5)
if mode == 'linger':
    w('ready\n')
    time.sleep(30)
    sys.exit(3)

exec 5>log-a 6>log-b 7>log-c 8>log-d 9>log-e
expect log_user > user-state
expect spawn /usr/bin/python3 tr.py -h fd -h pid
for l in 5 6 7 8; do expect log "$fd" -F $l -m; echo "log$l=$?" >> rcs; done
expect log "$fd" -F 9 -m 2> err; echo "log9=$?" >> rcs

expect log_user off; expect log_user >> user-state

expect expect "$fd" 'p2> ' -t 10 > out-off; echo "p2=$?" >> rcs
expect send "$fd" $'two\n'
expect expect "$fd" 'p3> ' -t 10 >> out-off; echo "p3=$?" >> rcs

expect sendline "$fd" three

expect eof "$fd" -t 10; echo "eof=$?" >> rcs
expect close "$fd" "$pid"; echo "close=$?" >> rcs

cases.purpose: A crypto secret handle (crypto secret-read from a run-time generated file) is delivered by send-secret to a spawned child that reads with ECHO off: the child's line equals the secret exactly. Malformed ('abc'), unknown ('15:999') and scrubbed handles are refused with the crypto diagnostic before that, writing nothing (else the child's line would not match exactly). The secret appears in neither the transcript log, expect's stdout (log_user on), nor the shell variable listing.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 mk.py
crypto secret-read -h H < pw; echo "read=$?" > rcs
crypto secret-read -h H2 < pw; crypto secret-scrub "$H2"; echo "scrub=$?" >> rcs
exec 5>log
expect spawn /usr/bin/python3 sec.py -h fd -h pid
expect log "$fd" -F 5 -m
expect expect "$fd" 'pass\? ' -t 10 > out; echo "prompt=$?" >> rcs
for h in abc 15:999 "$H2"; do
  expect send-secret "$fd" "$h" 2> err; echo "bad=$?" >> rcs
  [[ $(< err) == *'secret-write-fd: invalid handle' ]] && echo diagnosed >> rcs
done
expect send-secret "$fd" "$H"; echo "secret=$?" >> rcs
expect sendline "$fd" ''
expect expect "$fd" 'secret-match=[a-z]+ len=[0-9]+'$'\r' -t 10 -V res >> out; printf 'rc=%s %s\n' $? "${res%$'\r'}" >> rcs
expect eof "$fd" -t 10; expect close "$fd" "$pid"; echo "close=$?" >> rcs
exec 5>&-
set > vars
/usr/bin/python3 chk.py log out vars

secret = open('pw', 'rb').read().rstrip(b'\n')
